newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil denies creating credit lines for Bamerindus.
newsitem.headline: Brazil denies creating credit lines for Bamerindus.

text.p: Brazilian officials Tuesday said a report claiming the National Monetary Council (CMN) had set up special credit lines for ailing bank Bamerindus was wrong.

Central Bank Director of Monetary Policy Francisco Lopes said the credit lines had existed since 1994 and in no way could be said to favour any particular bank, the private Invest News agency reported.
Lopes said the report by financial columnist Celso Pinto claiming the CMN had resolved to bail out Bamerindus was "factually incorrect."
A Finance Ministry official echoed Lopes' denial, saying medium-term financial assistance was open to all comers and was not aimed at Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth-largest private bank.

Pinto wrote that the CMN last Thursday passed a resolution setting up the 90-day credit. He said the move was designed to allow Bamerindus' politically powerful majority shareholder, Sen. Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira, to solve the bank's liquidity problems and remain in control.
Lopes said the only modification that the CMN had carried out was to tie the special credit to a new interest rate, the TBAN, Invest News reported.
The TBAN, which comes into effect in October, is a higher, more punitive rate for rediscount lines drawn by banks to smooth over temporary liquidity problems.
It will be set at a slightly higher rate than the Basic Interest Rate of the Central Bank (TBC) and will be easier for institutions to draw.
